:::{#exr-matmul-distrib-proof}
#### Proving that matrix multiplication distributes from the left

@thm-matmul-distrib lets a [product](#def-matrix-mult) with a [matrix sum](#def-matrix-addition) be expanded term by term,
just as multiplication of numbers [distributes over](algebra.qmd#def-distributes-over) addition.
Let $\matr{A}$ be an $m \times k$ [matrix](#def-matrix),
and let $\matr{B}$ and $\matr{C}$ be $k \times n$ matrices.

Prove that $\matr{A}(\matr{B} + \matr{C}) = \matr{A}\matr{B} + \matr{A}\matr{C}$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Express the $(i, j)$ entry of the left side with @def-matrix-mult and @def-matrix-addition,
then split the result with [the rule for a sum of sums](algebra-sums.qmd#thm-sum-of-sums).

:::
